title: FakeProviderScript
description: Ordered sequence of pre-scripted ProviderResult responses driving a FakeProvider adapter (§9.1, §9.2, §6.14). Each entry binds by ordinal position to one `provider_adapter.invoke` call the runtime makes during the session; an optional `match` clause turns the binding into an asserted check that the entry was applied to the expected invocation context. The FakeProvider is shipped alongside the runtime as a normal `provider_adapter` per §6.1 / §6.11 — it conforms to the full §6 contract (`invoke(request) -> provider_result`, structured_output canonicalization, CLOSED `error.kind` enum, CLOSED `finish_reason` enum, usage reporting). The only differences from a real adapter are: no network call; the `ProviderResult` is read from this script; `usage` is exactly what the script provides; `structured_output` is pre-authored by the script (the §6.5 validation step still runs, so a deliberately-malformed entry exercises §4.9's `apply_agent_failure_policy`). FakeProvider determinism is unconditional under the §2.7 N3 qualifier: a fixed script and a fixed sequence of `ProviderRequest`s yields bit-identical ProviderResults across runs, on any host, because no LLM is invoked. FakeProvider is NOT a vendor name (rule N4); it is the spec's canonical name for the test adapter.

schema_version.description: Schema version per §5.1. The Pass 7 schema is `1.0.0`.

description.description: Human-readable description of the script's purpose (e.g. "two-round canonical session with one in-line fork and one deferred drain").

on_exhaustion.description: Behavior when the runtime makes more `invoke` calls than the script has entries. CLOSED enum. `error` (default): the FakeProvider returns a synthetic ProviderResult with `error.kind = internal` and `error.message = "fake_provider_script: entries exhausted"`, surfacing a script-too-short bug to the test. `loop`: the FakeProvider rewinds to `entries[0]`, allowing stress tests against a constant provider response.

entries.description: Ordered list of scripted responses. The N-th `invoke` call (counting in dispatch order across rounds, branches, and synthesis) receives `entries[N-1].result`. Order MUST be aligned with the runtime's declared-order dispatch (§4.10 invariant 2) and the §4.11 pseudocode flow: per round, the deferred-drain (if any) precedes panel primary_turns in declared order; each primary_turn may emit one in-line branch_turn before the next panel agent fires; the coordination_turn fires last in the round; an additional invocation for synthesis occurs on `verdict.next_action = finalize`.

match.description: Optional assertion fired before this entry's result is returned. If present, the FakeProvider checks every constraint against the inbound `ProviderRequest`; on mismatch the FakeProvider returns a synthetic ProviderResult with `error.kind = internal` and `error.message = "fake_provider_script: match assertion failed at entry <ordinal>: <constraint>"`. The runtime's §4.9 path then terminates the session with a `provider_unrecoverable` reason, surfacing the misalignment loudly to the test. If `match` is absent, the entry binds purely by ordinal position.

expected_output_schema.description: Asserts `ProviderRequest.expected_output_schema` equals this value. `null` (no structured output expected) has no MVP code path and is omitted here for that reason.

round.description: Asserts the round number derivable from the inbound request's context_packet (or from the FakeProvider's own invocation counter when the implementation exposes one). Implementation-defined visibility; RECOMMENDED for test richness, OPTIONAL for minimal harnesses.

turn_index.description: Asserts the turn_index derivable from the inbound request's context_packet. Same visibility caveat as `round`.

result.description: The ProviderResult the FakeProvider returns verbatim for this invocation. MUST validate against `provider_result.schema.json`. The script author is responsible for shape correctness; the FakeProvider does NOT mutate the result (other than the §6.5 structured_output validation that every adapter performs). To exercise a §6.6 `error.kind` value, populate `result.error` per the closed enum; to exercise a §6.4 tool lifecycle, populate `result.tool_events[]`; to exercise a malformed_response → §4.9 path, set `result.structured_output = null` and `result.error.kind = "malformed_response"`.

comment.description: Optional inline rationale for this entry (test documentation; not consumed by the FakeProvider).
